newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel prices track NYMEX higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel prices track NYMEX higher.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices rose Friday, fueled by a nearly one cent a gallon increase in front-month heating oil futures, traders said.
Differentials were steady in both Chicago and Group Three, where diesel inventories have been drawn down steadily over the past two weeks in the Williams pipeline system.

The Williams system, a key barometer of stocks in the Group market, reported a 29-day supply of low sulphur diesel and 24-day supply of gasoline on hand as trade wound down for the week, traders said.
Traders in the Midwest markets expected basis to remain steady next week, leaving prices to track NYMEX front-month futures absent any market-moving news.
"Basis probably will be steady even though diesel inventories have come down the past ten days," one trader said.
Chicago winter-grade unleaded gasoline remained 9.25/9.0 cents a gallon under NYMEX April unleaded, with summer-grade unleaded pegged between four and six cents firmer, traders said.
Group Three unleaded was bid 2.25 cents a gallon under the print for prompt barrels, with later deliveries 2.50 cent under, traders said.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was steady at 3.75/4.0 cents a gallon over April NYMEX heating oil for prompt deliveries and 3.50/3.75 cents a gallon over the print for later deliveries.
Group Three low sulphur diesel was talked 4.75/5.0 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 4.50/4.75 cents over the print for later deliveries, also unchanged.
